_doc: The canonical bytes a merchant signs to open a charge on dpay's own OpenCryptoPay checkout, and the ONE statement of that encoding outside dpay_core::CheckoutOpen. Two spellings live here: `golden` is the v2 buffer (domain dpay-checkout-open-v2) a request carrying a sale's `note` signs — the note rides its own u32-LE length prefix after the name — and `legacy_v1` is the frozen note-less buffer (domain dpay-checkout-open-v1) the wasm export w_checkout_open_sig must keep producing under the additive-only ABI policy. Emitted from the real core by `just wire-layout`; read back by crates/dpay-fixture (which rebuilds the golden struct from these offsets alone) and by scripts/check-wasm-core.mjs (which reproduces both buffers field-by-field in JS and checks the committed wasm's w_checkout_open_sig against legacy_v1.sig_hex and w_checkout_open_sig_note against golden.sig_hex). The relay verifies with dpay_core::validate_checkout_open, so it shares the encoding rather than a copy of it. Same convention as dfx/wire_layout.json — regenerated when the encoding deliberately changes, never hand-edited to make a test pass.
